classification.difficultyReason: Translate a physical relationship combining direct square variation and inverse variation, determine the constant, and substitute new values.

content.prompt: A model aeroplane attached to one end of a string moves in a horizontal circle. The tension, $T$ N (or newtons), in the string is directly proportional to the square of the speed, $v$ m/s, and inversely proportional to the radius, $r$ m, of the circle. If the radius is 10 m and the speed is 20 m/s, the tension is 60 N. Find the tension if the radius is 15 m and the speed is 30 m/s.

answer.worked:
$T\propto\dfrac{v^2}{r}$, so $T=\dfrac{kv^2}{r}$ for a positive constant $k$.

$$\begin{align*}60&=\frac{k\times20^2}{10}\\60&=40k\\k&=\frac32\end{align*}$$

Thus $T=\dfrac{3v^2}{2r}$. When $v=30$ and $r=15$:

$$\begin{align*}T&=\frac{3\times30^2}{2\times15}\\T&=90\text{ N}\end{align*}$$
